title: GTM checklist and release synchronization for Dedicated capacity: new regions, instance families, and reservation bundles
creator: Claire Chen
summary: Coordinate cross-functional go-to-market activities for the Dedicated capacity launch that introduces two new regions, two instance families, and a tiered reservation bundle product.
description:
Purpose: Prepare a single synchronized GTM runbook and release notes package for Dedicated capacity additions: EU-North-2 and APAC-SIN regions, new instance families (g6i and r6i equivalents), and tiered reservation bundles (standard, business, enterprise).

Scope: Customer-facing release notes, Console copy and rollout toggles, billing & metering validation, sales and support enablement materials, marketing announcement assets, and coordinated canary rollout with engineering. This ticket consolidates the cross-team checklist, owners, timeline, and pre/post-launch success metrics.

Why unique: Unlike prior region-only playbooks, this launch ties together SKU changes (new instance types + reservation bundles) that require billing, quota changes, console UX updates, and special migration notes for existing reservation customers. The objective is a friction-free purchase path and predictable customer experience during the canary to 100% rollout.
checklist: Finalize reservation SKUs and pricing tiers with Finance
Lock in supported instance types and exact GPU SKU names
Billing integration: ensure meter IDs, invoices and tax logic (ENG-4120)
Console: add region selector defaults and reservation purchase flow copy
Docs: write reservation FAQ, migration guide, and region availability map
Release notes: draft customer-facing copy + internal short-form for sales/support
SDK/CLI: surface new region flags and reservation APIs; update changelog
Sales enablement: prepare pitch deck, pricing calculator, objection handling
Support enablement: runbook for failure modes and entitlement checks
Monitoring: pre-launch dashboards for capacity, latency, error rates
Canary plan: 2-week canary in EU-North-2 for standard bundles, automated fallback to hosted API on overload
Runbook rehearsal: tabletop with Eng/SRE/Support/ProdMgmt before soft launch
Legal/regulatory review: confirm data residency language for APAC-SIN
Marketing: finalize announcement copy, blog, and launch webinar date
Post-launch: 14-day usage/economics review and migration support window
timeline: 2026-03-10: Console flows implemented and design sign-off
2026-03-14: Internal dry-run tabletop and canary plan finalized
2026-03-16: Start 2-week canary in EU-North-2 (standard bundles only)
2026-03-23: Canary review; expand to APAC-SIN if no high-severity issues
2026-03-28: Full launch - region flags enabled, reservation purchases open
release_notes_draft:
Announcing Dedicated capacity in EU-North-2 and APAC-SIN + new reservation bundles.

What’s new: Dedicated capacity is now available in EU-North-2 and APAC-SIN. We’re also introducing two new instance families (g6i-equivalent for throughput-focused workloads and r6i-equivalent for memory-intensive models) plus tiered reservation bundles: Standard (pay-as-you-reserve baseline), Business (discounted token rates + burst credits), Enterprise (SLA + dedicated support + volume discounts).

Who this is for: Customers who need predictable throughput and isolation, or want to optimize unit economics with reservations. Existing Dedicated customers can purchase new reservations via the Console; see the migration guide for mapping existing commitments.

Notes: Metering and invoices will reference new SKU codes (see Billing section in docs). If you’re on an existing reservation, review the migration FAQ before purchasing to avoid unexpected overlaps.

Support: For help, contact support@redwood.ai or open a Support ticket via Console.
comms_plan:
Channels: #gtm-dedicated Slack channel for real-time triage, bi-daily 15m standups during canary, weekly cross-functional syncs pre-launch.
Audience & cadence: Internal announcement to Sales, Support, and CSMs 48 hours before full launch; Marketing embargoed assets delivered 24 hours before public blog; Partner marketplace listings coordinated with Channel Ops.
Owner: Product (Claire Chen) coordinates with Marketing (Zoe Martin) to publish blog and webinar registration.
Escalation: Any Sev2+ issue during canary triggers immediate rollback of reservation purchases and page banner; postmortem required within 72 hours.
risks_mitigation: Risk: Billing mismatch for reservation SKUs -> Mitigation: End-to-end invoice test cases and finance sign-off before open purchases
Risk: Console purchase flow confusion -> Mitigation: Simplified copy, inline help, and full-screen demo in sales enablement
Risk: Capacity starvation in canary -> Mitigation: Autoscale burst policy + automated fallback to hosted model variants
Risk: Data residency compliance questions in APAC -> Mitigation: Legal review and explicit residency copy in docs
Risk: Unexpected cost regression for high-throughput customers -> Mitigation: Pre-launch quotas and early-adopter credits
success_metrics: Customer adoption: % of existing Dedicated customers purchasing new reservations within 30 days
Revenue: MRR attributable to reservation bundles in first 60 days
Reliability: P95 request latency remains within SLA across new regions
Support: Number of reservation-related support tickets in first 14 days
Billing accuracy: 0 critical invoice discrepancies reported in first billing cycle
Cost: Measured cost-per-token for reserved workloads vs hosted baseline
post_launch_tasks: Run 14-day economic analysis and share findings with Finance and GTM
Schedule customer interviews for top 10 reservation purchasers
Ship follow-up console UX improvements based on support logs
Close feedback loop with Runtime team for any perf regressions
Publish post-launch FAQ and migration case studies
